title: How Unlikely Is "Unlikely"? Assessing Verbal Probability Perception Across Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.26327v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models increasingly produce and interpret verbal probability expressions, yet whether these expressions carry consistent meaning across models (or match human perceptions of uncertainty) remains unknown. We present a systematic cross-model evaluation using a word-to-number mapping task grounded in established human benchmarks. Eleven uncertainty expressions were presented to 19 models under two conditions, forced single-number response and explanation elicitation, alongside a novel bidirectional roundtrip test of internal consistency. LLMs track the human benchmark with surprising fidelity: word ordering is preserved, three anchor points are recovered, and ``possible'' shows the highest variance and cross-model disagreement of any expression tested, consistent with its documented bimodal interpretation in humans. However, models show a systematic upward bias for negative expressions such as ``unlikely'' and ``improbable.

translated_title: “不可能”有多不可能？评估大型语言模型中的概率言语感知
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型越来越多地生成和解释言语概率表达，但这些表达在模型间是否具有一致含义（或是否与人类对不确定性的感知相匹配）仍属未知。我们基于已有的人类基准，通过词到数字映射任务进行了一项系统的跨模型评估。在两种条件下——强制单一数字回答和解释引出——向19个模型呈现了11种不确定性表达，并辅以一项新颖的双向往返测试以检验内部一致性。大型语言模型以惊人的保真度追踪人类基准：词语排序得以保留，三个锚点被恢复，且“可能”在所有测试表达中显示出最高的方差和跨模型分歧，这与人类中记录的其双峰解释相一致。然而，模型对“不可能”和“不太可能”等否定表达表现出系统性向上偏差。
tldr: 大型语言模型在理解概率词语时与人类基准高度一致，但对否定表达（如“不可能”）存在系统性高估偏差，且“可能”一词在模型间分歧最大。
en_tdlr: Large language models closely align with human benchmarks in interpreting probability words, but show a systematic upward bias for negative expressions like "unlikely," while "possible" exhibits the highest cross-model disagreement.
